3.happening: We create the list of course nodes.
3.why: The prerequisites form a directed graph of courses.

4.why: Each course is a graph vertex.

5.happening: We append a node for this course.
5.why: It becomes a vertex in the graph.
5.invariant: Every course has exactly one node.

6.why: Each prerequisite is a directed edge.
6.invariant: Edges point from prerequisite to dependent.

7.why: DFS needs each node's outgoing neighbours.
7.invariant: adj[b] lists courses that require b.

8.happening: We prepare an empty neighbour list per course.
8.why: Neighbours are added as prerequisites are read.
8.invariant: Every course starts with no neighbours.

9.happening: We start course {i}'s neighbour list empty.
9.why: It fills as prerequisites are processed.
9.invariant: adj has one list per course.

11.invariant: a cannot be taken before its prerequisite.

12.invariant: b must be taken before a.

14.happening: We record {a} as a neighbour of {b}.

15.why: DFS colours nodes white, grey, or black.
15.invariant: Colour tracks each node's DFS state.

17.why: No course has been visited yet.

18.happening: We assume there is no cycle.
18.why: A cycle is proven only by a back-edge.
18.invariant: has_cycle is False until a back-edge appears.

19.happening: There is no current node yet.
19.why: cur is set only during DFS.

20.happening: We start scanning courses for a DFS root.

21.happening: We consider course {start} as a DFS root.
21.why: Disconnected parts each need their own DFS.
21.invariant: Courses before start are already handled.

22.happening: Course {start} is white — start a DFS here.
22.why: Only unvisited courses begin a new DFS.
22.invariant: Each node is rooted at most once.

22.happening: Course {start} was already visited — skip it.
22.why: It belongs to an earlier DFS tree.

23.happening: We seed the DFS stack with course {start}.
23.why: The stack drives the iterative DFS.
23.invariant: The stack holds the current DFS path plus pending nodes.

24.happening: The DFS stack still has {len(stack)} node(s).
24.why: DFS continues until the stack empties.
24.invariant: Every stacked node is eventually finished.

24.happening: The DFS stack is empty — this tree is done.

25.why: DFS processes the deepest pending node.
25.invariant: The top of the stack is the deepest node.

26.why: It is the node being processed.

27.happening: This is the first visit to course {node_id}.
27.invariant: A white node becomes grey on first visit.

27.why: Its neighbours are done, so it can finish.
27.invariant: A grey node finishes on its second visit.

28.happening: We colour course {node_id} grey (on the current path).
28.why: Grey marks nodes in the active DFS path.
28.invariant: A back-edge is an edge to a grey node.

29.invariant: Every neighbour is inspected once per expansion.

30.why: It might extend the path or reveal a cycle.
30.invariant: nb is a course that requires node_id.

31.happening: Neighbour {nb} is grey — a back-edge, so there is a cycle!
31.why: An edge to a node on the current path closes a loop.
31.invariant: A grey target means the courses cannot all be taken.

31.happening: Neighbour {nb} is not grey, so no back-edge here.
31.why: Only grey targets indicate a cycle.
31.invariant: White or black neighbours are safe.

32.happening: We record that a cycle exists.

33.happening: Neighbour {nb} is white — push it to explore.
Neighbour {nb} is already seen, so it is not pushed.
33.why: Grey and black nodes need no re-exploration.
33.invariant: Each node is pushed for exploration once.

34.happening: We push neighbour {nb} onto the DFS stack.
34.invariant: The stack grows deeper along the path.

36.happening: All of course {node_id}'s neighbours are done — colour it black.
36.why: Black means fully explored and safe.
36.invariant: A black node leaves the current path.

37.happening: We pop the finished node off the stack.
37.why: It is done and off the path.
37.invariant: The stack shrinks as nodes finish.

38.happening: We clear the current node between components.
38.why: No node is current while scanning for the next root.

39.happening: We move to the next course.
39.why: Every course must be rooted or skipped.

40.happening: The answer is true only if no cycle was found.
40.why: A cycle makes the schedule impossible.
40.invariant: result is the negation of has_cycle.

41.why: It says whether all courses can be finished.
41.invariant: A cycle-free graph can always be finished.

init.happening: Build the prerequisite graph and colour all courses white.

loop.happening: Root a DFS or expand the stack.
loop.why: Every course is visited via DFS.
loop.invariant: Grey nodes form the current path.

check.happening: Test a root, a first visit, or a back-edge.
check.why: These drive exploration and cycle detection.
check.invariant: A grey neighbour means a cycle.

update.happening: Colour a node, record a cycle, or push a neighbour.

move.happening: Peek, pop, or advance the scan.
move.why: The stack and scan move deterministically.

return.happening: Return whether the courses can be finished.
return.invariant: The verdict follows from cycle detection.
